item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract and has much better scope discipline, although it still needs correction before merge.","reasons":["A reuses the established multipartbody.NewFile helper directly and adds only the requested Upload API.","A keeps FilesOption semantics unchanged and avoids the association APIs and multipart helper expansion explicitly forbidden by the contract.","A centralizes request construction and response handling in a shared add helper, whereas B duplicates the full Add request/decoding path inside Upload, creating drift risk and violating the requirement to route through Add.","A tests the multipart field, filename, content, and retrying streamed file content. B has stronger validation/error tests, but much of its added implementation and test surface supports out-of-scope association functionality."],"risks_a":["A changes Add behavior by eagerly reading and buffering every caller-provided body, contrary to the requirement to preserve Add behavior.","Upload calls the private add helper rather than the existing Add method, so it does not literally satisfy the required routing pattern.","The added tests do not cover Upload validation or source-reader failures as required; the validation also combines two cases into one less-specific error."],"risks_b":["B adds six exported association options and form-field behavior despite the explicit instruction not to add association fields or change FilesOption behavior.","B expands multipartbody with Field and NewFileWithFields instead of using the existing NewFile helper as requested.","Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error handling instead of routing through Add, increasing maintenance risk and violating the centralization requirement."]}
